What are sales KPIs in HubSpot and why do they matter?

A sales KPI, or key performance indicator, is a measurable metric that indicates how well a team is achieving its goals, such as revenue growth, average deal size, or pipeline velocity. Consistent KPI definitions give executives, managers, and reps the same numbers, so performance reviews focus on decisions instead of reconciling reports.

In HubSpot, KPI dashboards pull from your CRM data and update automatically. Reports built with the custom report builder refresh every two hours, and managers can refresh manually every 15 minutes, so they can review pipeline and revenue figures without rebuilding a report each time. Because sales, marketing, and service data live in the same CRM, teams can build one dashboard from a shared source instead of combining exports.
HubSpot Smart CRM provides connected customer and deal data to support KPI reporting, while Sales Hub provides reporting, dashboards, goals, and forecasting.
Leading vs. Lagging Sales KPIs in HubSpot
Leading KPIs show activity and pipeline movement before a sale, while lagging KPIs show results after deals progress or close. HubSpot reporting can combine both across CRM objects and properties.

A property is a single field on a record, such as a deal amount. A KPI is a calculation built from one or more properties. For example, quarterly closed-won revenue is a KPI calculated from deal properties, deal stage, and close date.

These areas also reflect current sales priorities. In HubSpot’s 2026 State of Sales report, 21% of sales leaders named improved deal tracking and management their top priority, while 20% prioritized improving conversion rates and 17% prioritized pipeline generation.

Teams might need additional properties if the sales process uses custom qualification stages, territories, product lines, or revenue definitions. The KPI definition should determine the fields in the report, rather than relying on whichever properties are available.
How to Build Sales KPIs in HubSpot Dashboards

Build each KPI from the underlying CRM data before adding it to a dashboard. A polished sales dashboard won’t fix a report that uses the wrong property, includes the wrong deals, or calculates a KPI differently from another team.

This is especially important after a CRM migration, when legacy fields, duplicate properties, and different pipeline definitions can affect reporting. Start by confirming the data behind each KPI, then build and validate the report before adding it to the dashboard.
Choose or create properties for each KPI.
First, list the data required to calculate each KPI. Win rate, for example, requires both the deal stage and the close date. For the pipeline created, include the deal amount and the create date.
Teams can use HubSpot’s default properties when they already capture the needed data. Check existing properties before creating custom ones. If a KPI requires data unique to your sales process:
Select the CRM object, such as Deal properties.
Add the property name and select the appropriate field type.
Configure any required rules or validation, then create the property.
For example, an enterprise team might create properties for sales region, product line, or a custom qualification stage.
Avoid creating a new property when HubSpot already stores the required value. Duplicate fields can split the data used for the same KPI.
Create saved reports for each KPI.

Once the required data is available, create one saved report for each KPI. Sales analytics in Sales Hub Professional and Enterprise provides reporting views for pipeline, revenue, prospecting activity, and sales performance. Start with a pre-built report when one matches your KPI, then use the custom report builder when you need different fields or cross-object data.
When the capability is available and enabled, HubSpot can also generate AI descriptions for reports. Go to Reporting > Reports > Sales and select the report closest to the KPI you need. Then:
Set the relevant date range and pipeline.
Filter by reps, teams, or other required properties.
Add any additional filters needed for your KPI definition.
Check that the report returns the expected records.
Click Save report and add it to your KPI dashboard.
For KPIs that a pre-built report cannot calculate, use HubSpot’s custom report builder to select the required data sources and fields. Custom reports can be saved directly to a dashboard.
Name reports consistently so users know exactly what they measure. For example: Win Rate_Enterprise_North America instead of Enterprise Sales Report.
Add saved KPI reports to a dashboard under Reporting > Dashboards. You can also add an existing report from Reporting > Reports by selecting Actions > Add to dashboard.

Organize the dashboard around how the team reviews performance. Put headline KPIs such as revenue and quota attainment first. Follow them with reports that explain pipeline movement, conversion, and rep performance. Then add dashboard-level filters for dimensions users need to compare regularly, such as:

In HubSpot, select Advanced filters > Add filter, then choose the property you want to filter by. Dashboard filters can apply across compatible reports, so users can change the view without editing each report separately.

Set dashboard access based on who needs to view or change the reports. HubSpot supports view-only or editing access. Enterprise accounts can assign access to specific users and teams. Dashboard emails can also be scheduled instead of relying on stakeholders to open HubSpot manually.
Open the dashboard and select Share > Email this dashboard.
Choose a daily, weekly, or monthly schedule.
Select Send with current dashboard filters if the email should preserve the filtered view.

Recurring dashboard emails use the permissions of the person who creates them. If each sales manager should receive only their own data, have each manager create their own recurring email. Note: Recurring dashboard emails can only be sent to HubSpot users.
How to Map Dynamics 365 KPIs to Sales KPIs in HubSpot

Don’t assume a Dynamics 365 metric and a similarly named HubSpot metric use the same records or calculation. Document the source definition first, then map its fields, stage rules, dates, and ownership logic to HubSpot.
Use a KPI mapping table during migration and validate each result against a known reporting period before replacing the Dynamics report.

HubSpot’s stage-history properties can help preserve more detailed pipeline KPIs. Properties such as Date entered [stage], Date exited [stage], and Cumulative time in [stage] support stage conversion and sales velocity reporting when the required history is available.

Pay attention to Amount and Close date during validation. HubSpot can calculate deal amount from line items using measures such as TCV, ACV, ARR, or MRR. Its close date can also be updated automatically when a deal enters the closed stage. Those rules should match the KPI definition agreed during migration before comparing HubSpot results with historical Dynamics reports.

Once the migrated KPIs are validated, include the new reports and dashboards in post-migration Sales Hub onboarding. Reps need to understand which fields they own and when to update them, while managers need to know which reports replace their previous Dynamics views.
How to Set Targets for Sales KPIs in HubSpot

Set targets so sales managers can compare actual KPI performance against the expected result for a given period. In HubSpot, you can assign sales goals to individual users, teams, or teams with individual user targets.
Sales Hub brings goals, KPI reporting, and forecasting together so managers can compare targets with current performance and expected pipeline outcomes.

Before creating a goal, define who owns the target, the reporting period, and which pipeline should count toward it. For example, a regional sales team should only be measured against the pipeline and revenue it owns.
Go to Reporting > Goals > Create goal. You can create a goal from a HubSpot template or, with supported subscriptions, build a custom goal. Then:
Choose the sales goal you want to measure.
Name the goal and select its contributors.
Choose individual users, team goals only, or teams with individual user targets.
Set the duration, such as monthly or quarterly.
Enter the target for each user or team.
Assign the appropriate pipeline where applicable.
Review the targets and save the goal.
Use individual goals when reps own separate quotas. Use team goals when performance is evaluated collectively. Choose team and individual targets when managers need both views.
Permissions also affect who can manage goals. Creating, editing, and deleting sales goals requires an eligible Sales or Service Hub seat or Super Admin access.

HubSpot can notify users when specified goal milestones are reached. During goal setup, select the milestones that should trigger a notification before saving the goal. For existing goals, open Reporting > Goals, select the goal, and edit its notification settings.
Keep notifications tied to milestones that require attention. A manager may need an alert when a rep reaches a target, while routine progress can stay in the dashboard.
How to Add Attribution and Cross-Functional KPIs in HubSpot

Sales KPIs can show that pipeline or revenue changed, but sales data alone may not explain why. That matters when 20% of sales leaders rank improving sales and marketing alignment as one of their top priorities for 2026. Attribution and cross-functional KPIs connect sales results with the marketing activity that contributed to pipeline and the customer data generated after the sale.

HubSpot Smart CRM connects customer data across Sales Hub, Marketing Hub, and Service Hub. That lets sales leaders add marketing attribution and post-sale KPIs to the same reporting environment they already use for pipeline and revenue. For example, you can report on:
Marketing contribution: Compare leads, opportunities, or revenue by campaign and original traffic source.
Revenue attribution: Identify which marketing or sales interactions contributed to revenue.
Customer retention: Monitor retention alongside new revenue to see how much business the company keeps after acquisition.
Customer experience: Add service KPIs such as ticket volume or response time to account and revenue reporting.

Choose cross-functional KPIs based on the question you need to answer. If pipeline falls, source and campaign data can show whether fewer qualified leads are reaching sales. If revenue rises while retention falls, post-sale data shows that new business is not translating into retained customers.
How to Ensure Data Quality for Sales KPIs in HubSpot
Duplicate deals can inflate pipeline, missing amounts can understate revenue, and inconsistent stages can distort conversion rates, so each KPI depends on the integrity of the records behind it.
For more complex reporting environments, Data Hub can support this work with reusable datasets, data-quality tooling, automation, and connections to external data sources.
Assign one person or team to own KPI data quality. That owner should maintain field definitions, review exceptions, and approve changes that affect reporting.

Reduce variation in how sales data is entered into HubSpot. Start with the properties used in your KPI calculations and define what each field means, when it must be completed, and which values users can select. HubSpot’s CRM customization capabilities let teams adapt properties, objects, and record layouts to match their sales process. For example:
Use controlled dropdown options instead of free-text fields for data such as region, deal type, and loss reason
Make key information required at the appropriate deal stage, such as amount or close date
Define clear entry and exit criteria for every pipeline stage
Merge duplicate CRM records so the same customer or opportunity is not counted twice
Restrict property and pipeline changes to users responsible for CRM governance

Duplicate contacts can also fragment activity and attribution across multiple records. HubSpot’s contact management tools store customer records in a centralized CRM database to maintain a consistent record for reporting, and duplicate management helps you merge records that overlap. For contact and company data that is missing or outdated, data enrichment can populate and refresh record fields without relying entirely on manual updates.
Review these rules after a migration as well. A legacy Dynamics field may have been mapped to a HubSpot property with different options or reporting logic.

Create saved views or reports that surface records likely to affect KPI accuracy. Useful checks include deals with no amount, overdue close dates, missing owners, duplicate records, and deals sitting in one stage beyond the expected timeframe.
For more complex reporting, HubSpot datasets let teams prepare reusable collections of CRM data, helping RevOps apply the same underlying data logic across reports.
Set a review cadence based on how quickly the underlying data changes. Pipeline and deal-stage data may need frequent checks, while slower-moving fields can be reviewed less often.

The named data owner should investigate exceptions and document any changes to KPI definitions or fields. This keeps data-quality fixes from becoming one-off cleanups and gives teams a clear point of accountability when a dashboard number looks wrong.
How to Roll Out Sales KPIs in HubSpot to Executives and Teams

The same dashboard should not serve every audience. Executives need enough information to make resource and revenue decisions, while managers and reps need more detail to act on performance. Create separate HubSpot dashboards for each audience, then define what they need to see and how often they should review it.
Keep the executive view focused on overall sales performance and risks that require leadership action.
Decisions: Are we on track to hit revenue targets? Is there enough pipeline to support future targets? Where is performance falling behind?
Metrics: Revenue, quota attainment, sales variance between actual and target performance, pipeline value, win rate, sales cycle length, and forecast.
Filters: Region, business unit, product line, and reporting period.
Permissions: Give leadership view access while limiting editing rights to the reporting or RevOps owners.
Review cadence: Review monthly or quarterly, with more frequent checks during forecasting periods.
Managers need enough detail to identify where performance is slipping and which reps or deals need attention.
Decisions: Which deals need intervention? Where is pipeline slowing? Which reps are ahead of or behind target?
Metrics: Pipeline created, stage conversion, deal velocity (how long individual deals spend in each stage), win rate, quota attainment, rep activity, and forecast.
Filters: Team, rep, pipeline, deal stage, and reporting period.
Permissions: Give managers access to the teams and records they manage, with editing limited to approved dashboard owners where needed.
Review cadence: Review weekly, using the same dashboard during pipeline and forecast meetings.
A rep dashboard should focus on the work and targets each seller can influence directly.
Decisions: Which opportunities need attention? Am I on track for quota? Where should I focus this week?
Metrics: Individual pipeline, quota attainment, open opportunities, upcoming close dates, stage progression, and sales activity.
Filters: Deal owner, pipeline, stage, and close date.
Permissions: Limit the view to the records and reports appropriate for each rep’s access level.
Review cadence: Check daily or before planning sales activity for the week.

Consistent KPI definitions improve trust in leadership reporting. If executives and managers calculate pipeline or win rate differently, they can see different results for the same period and spend review meetings reconciling numbers instead of discussing performance.
Pro tip: Reps can also use AI Guided Selling to surface leads, deals, tasks, and recommended next actions alongside the performance data managers track.
Governance Security and Enterprise Rollout For Sales KPIs in HubSpot

Enterprise KPI reporting needs controls around who can see the data and who can change the inputs behind it. Without those controls, a field edit or permission change can affect reports used across multiple teams. Start by defining access at three levels:
CRM records: Set view, edit, and delete permissions by user or team. HubSpot can limit users to their own records or records owned by their team.
Properties: Restrict access to properties used for sensitive or business-critical reporting. For example, limit who can edit fields used to calculate revenue or segment deals.
Reports and dashboards: Give teams access to the reporting assets they need without giving every user editing rights. Enterprise accounts can assign dashboard access to specific users and teams.

For larger organizations, use HubSpot teams to partition access and reporting by structures such as region or business unit. Enterprise accounts also support nested teams, so parent teams can see records owned by teams below them.

Keep ownership of KPI definitions, properties, pipelines, permissions, and dashboards with a small group of administrators or RevOps stakeholders. Document changes that affect KPI calculations, so teams know when a metric’s underlying logic has changed.
CIO and IT stakeholders planning CRM governance, security, integrations, and broader technology strategy can also use HubSpot’s CIO Resource Library for additional guidance.
Frequently Asked Questions About Sales KPIs in HubSpot
Which sales pipeline metrics should I prioritize first?

Prioritize metrics that show whether you have enough pipeline to meet your target and how efficiently that pipeline becomes revenue. Start with pipeline value, pipeline created, stage conversion rate, win rate, sales cycle length, and closed-won revenue. Add team-specific KPIs once these core metrics are defined consistently.
How do I handle multi-currency and multi-region KPI rollups in HubSpot?

HubSpot converts deal amounts into the specific company’s currency using the exchange rate set for the deal’s currency. Use the Amount in company currency property when reports need to combine deals across currencies. For regional reporting, use consistent properties for region or territory and apply them as report or dashboard filters.
What is the best way to set and manage quarterly targets in HubSpot?

Create quarterly goals in HubSpot and assign them to the individual users or teams responsible for the target. Set the correct pipeline where applicable, then compare goal progress with the same KPI reports managers use during pipeline and forecast reviews.
When should you create custom properties for sales KPIs in HubSpot?

Create a custom property when the KPI depends on business-specific data that HubSpot does not already capture. Examples include a custom territory, qualification status, or deal classification. Check HubSpot’s default properties first to avoid creating duplicate fields that split reporting data.
How do I migrate KPI definitions from Dynamics 365 to HubSpot reliably?

Document each Dynamics KPI before rebuilding it in HubSpot, including its source fields, calculation, stage logic, date rules, and ownership rules. Map those elements to HubSpot properties, then compare both systems over the same historical period. Investigate discrepancies before making the HubSpot report the new reporting baseline.
